title: The reduction tower of a complex is normalized
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For any scheme $T$, work on a small skeleton of its pro-étale site in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and put $R_T=\mathcal O_{E,T}=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T$ and $R_{T,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T$, as in [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(R_T)$ of sheaves of $R_T$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $M\in D(R_T)$ the reductions
$$M/\ell^n=M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_T}R_{T,n}$$
form an object $\operatorname{red}_TM$ of $D(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$, functorial in $M$, with these evaluations and quotient-induced transitions [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. All its reduction maps
$$ (M/\ell^n)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{R_{T,n}}R_{T,m}\longrightarrow M/\ell^m\qquad(1\leq m\leq n)$$
are isomorphisms.

Here $\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ and $\Dctf(T,\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)$ mean bounded complexes with constructible cohomology and their finite-Tor subcategories over the pulled-back coefficient sheaves, as in [sk-def-sfb-constructible, det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]; the completed integral sheaf is the $R_T$ above. Assume now that $T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. If $M\in\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$, then
$$\operatorname{red}_TM\in\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)_{\mathrm{norm}}$$
[sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], where finite-level constructibility means [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. More precisely $M$ has finite Tor amplitude, and every interval $[a,b]$ of Tor amplitude for $M$ is an interval of Tor amplitude, and of cohomological support, for every level $M/\ell^n$.

proof.text: The abelian coefficient comparison is multiplicative. Reconstruct its section rings using the internal/section module interface; on sections this retains precisely spIntegralAbComparison. The two private proved helpers construct this ring isomorphism without choosing an arbitrary existence witness.

Apply the fixed-presentation strict descent theorem to this coefficient-ring isomorphism, obtaining the ordinary and derived functors, level and evaluation isomorphisms, strict quotient transitions and universal K-flat computation counit.
Apply the adjunct comparison to obtain invertibility of every D.reduction at every red(M), without qcqs.

For qcqs T and bounded constructible internalization of M, apply the Tor interval theorem and the finite-level constructibility theorem. Choose a finite Tor interval [a,b] and widen its lower endpoint to min(a,b) so the interval is ordered. The interval theorem supplies that same Tor and cohomological bound at every level.

Assemble the actual SpReductionTower fields. At each level combine its common cohomology interval, constructible homology and finite Tor amplitude. Use those same two ordered endpoints for the common tower bounds, and adjoin the normalization from step 3. Retain the interval theorem for the arbitrary-Tor-interval clause.

proof_origin.place: Construction, normalization, and constructibility assertions; final Tor-amplitude sentence

blueprint_update.statement:
For $M\in D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$ the reductions
$M/\ell^n=M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^n$ form an
object $\operatorname{red}_TM=(M/\ell^n)_n$ of
$D(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$, functorial in $M$, whose reduction maps
are isomorphisms. If $M\in\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$, then
$\operatorname{red}_TM\in\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)_{\mathrm{norm}}$
([sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]), with the Tor amplitude bounds of $M$.

proof.text:
*Construction.* Choose a functorial K-flat representative $P$ of $M$ over
$\mathcal O_{E,T}$. The strict complexes $P\otimes_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^n$
with the maps induced by the quotients
$\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^{n+1}\to\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^n$ form a complex of towers,
defining $\operatorname{red}_TM\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$; quasi-isomorphisms
of K-flat complexes give levelwise quasi-isomorphisms, so this is functorial in
$M$. Its level $n$ is $M/\ell^n$ by exactness of evaluation
([det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]).

*Normalization.* For $m\leq n$, the reduction map is the associativity
isomorphism
$(P\otimes\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^n)\otimes_{\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^n}\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^m
\cong P\otimes\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^m$ (the left side computes the derived
tensor product, $P\otimes\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^n$ being K-flat over
$\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^n$), hence an isomorphism.

*Constructibility.* Let $M\in\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$. By [sk-lem-int-integral-heart],
$M$ is a finite extension of shifted sheaves $a_!C$ with $C$ of Tor amplitude
$[-1,0]$ on a stratum. Tor amplitude and constructibility of the reductions are
preserved by extensions and shifts, and the number of steps and the shifts do
not depend on $n$. Hence $M$ has finite Tor amplitude, say in $[a,b]$, and each
$M/\ell^n$ lies in $\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)$ with Tor amplitude
in $[a,b]$. Since $M/\ell^n$ has
Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ and is bounded, its cohomology lies in $[a,b]$ as
well (Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ forces the cohomology to vanish outside it).
So the cohomological and Tor bounds are independent of $n$.
